text:
emma_hr: Heads up - need routing and quick clarity on an offer exception for a UK-based new hire joining from Ireland on 2025-04-28. Manager is asking for a one-time comp uplift (pro-rata for Q2) plus a split payroll for month 1 because the relocation/bridge stipend will land after payroll cutoff. Can we confirm approval path and if this is allowed under current comp policies?

emma_hr: Context and numbers below:
```
Base comp band midpoint: A372,000
Offered base: A375,000 (within band)
Manager asking temporary uplift: +A36,000 for Q2 only (pro-rata: A33,000 for two months)
Relocation bridge stipend: A34,500 (one-time) - expected to be paid after final relocation invoice ~2 weeks after start
Requested split: pay employee base for first month on standard payroll, then pay remaining base + bridge stipend on next payroll cycle to align with cashflow.
Tax note: employee will be UK-tax resident on start; need confirmation if stipend is taxable as earnings or reimbursed expense.
```

sam_comp: @emma_hr thanks for the details. Quick notes: 1) Any uplift that materially changes OTE or moves candidate outside approved band requires comp committee sign-off. 2) For a one-time, time-limited uplift (Q2 only) we can approve provisionally if manager + recruiting lead + finance agree and comp ops stamps it as 'temporary adjustment'. 3) Please route to comp-approvals@redwood and include manager rationale + org chart. :eyes:

dina_peopleops: Also need the signed offer letter copy and confirmation of start date. If we split payroll we must note it on the offer so candidate knows exact timing. HR will not backdate benefits eligibility - benefits eligibility date remains start date unless Benefits team approves.

legal_bot: Flag for payroll/tax: relocation bridge likely taxable unless paid as a direct vendor reimbursement. If it flows through payroll, payroll will withhold. If it's a vendor reimbursement (company pays hotel directly), we can treat it as non-taxable. Please run through payroll and finance for classification.

raj_payroll: Splitting month 1 pay is doable but has constraints: payroll cutoff is the 20th for the month. If employee starts 28-Apr, first run pays pro-rated base for Apr on May payroll; second run can include the remainder + stipend on next cycle (June). Need new-hire paperwork in by 2025-04-22 to hit May cycle. For tax reporting, two payments in the same tax month are fine; we'll need a note in payroll that the second payment is a one-time adjustment. Also need vendor invoice or expense code if stipend is being reimbursed.

marta_finance: Finance ok to cover a one-time temporary uplift as a hiring incentive under GL 6101 (hiring adjustments) but we need: 1) manager approval email, 2) comp-approvals confirmation, 3) a PO or one-time approval for the stipend if paid to employee. If the stipend is taxable and paid through payroll, we will remit PAYE/NIC accordingly. Please cc finance-ops@redwood on the approval thread.

emma_hr: Quick question - is manager approval + comp-approvals email chain enough to avoid full committee if we mark it as 'temporary incentive < A310k'?

sam_comp: If total incremental spend (uplift + stipend) is under A310k and manager + recruiting lead + finance sign off, comp ops can rubber-stamp without full committee. Document the pro-rate calculation and expiration date.

dina_peopleops: I'll draft the offer amendment language for the split payment and temporary uplift and share here for sign-off.

emma_hr: Thanks all - I'll prepare the comp-approvals email with attachments (offer draft, manager rationale, pro-rate calc) and loop in finance-ops + payroll. Will post the email thread here once sent. :thumbsup:
